public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no future for any AI company that uses a subscription-based approach without directly passing on the cost of compute.
conditions: subscription-based AI companies that don't directly pass on the cost of compute

statement.excerpt: In any case, there is no future for any AI company that uses a subscription-based approach, at least not one where they don’t directly pass on the cost of compute.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: don’t directly pass on the cost of compute
our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts that AI businesses cannot remain commercially viable with fixed subscriptions that absorb variation in customers' compute use.
Commercial viability requires sustained operations supported by the business's economics. Continued operation financed by new investment alone does not establish it.
Ordinary usage caps do not automatically constitute direct compute-cost billing; the post itself discusses capped subscriptions.
The universal wording includes AI companies beyond Anthropic and OpenAI, although those companies dominate the context.
This is a qualitative business-model prediction, with no stated financial metric or accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence shows that businesses using the specified model fail or must abandon it because its economics cannot support continued operation. Individual failures would establish only those cases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one qualifying AI business demonstrates sustained commercial viability while retaining subscriptions that do not directly bill customers for their compute consumption.
